prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Mixed · Multilingual glossary (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 76px · one-line width 165px
  col 2: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 62px
  col 3: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 107px
  col 4: header "한국어" · longest unbreakable word 13px · one-line width 73px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 112px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [104, 54, 70, 60, 71] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [98, 53, 69, 60, 79] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [98, 67, 64, 65, 65] · table 360×405px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 83, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [98, 62, 68, 66, 65] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [98, 65, 65, 66, 65] · table 360×405px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 83, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [111, 58, 68, 57, 65] · table 360×381px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [97, 56, 78, 63, 65] · table 360×335px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [105, 58, 68, 58, 70] · table 360×381px · row heights [60, 36, 60, 60, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r1B"],"acceptable":["r1C","r2B","r3B"],"bad":[{"design":"r2A","why":"日本語 splits into 日本 / 語 in the header, doubling the header row to 60px; the starved Japanese column then pushes 列幅の割り当て to four lines, giving the tallest table in the set (405px)."},{"design":"r2C","why":"Same faults as r2A — broken 日本語 header, 60px header row, a 4-line cell and 405px total height — with no compensating gain elsewhere."},{"design":"r3A","why":"한국어 breaks into 한국 / 어 in the header while the Korean body column is the narrowest (57px), so Korean cells wrap to three lines (가로 스크롤, 열 너비 할당) even though English is over-fed at 111px."},{"design":"r3C","why":"한국어 again splits across two header lines (col 4 = 58px) and the header row grows to 60px, so the table is 381px tall for no benefit over r1B."}],"contrast":{"widths":[72,72,72,72,71],"why":"The plausible 'just divide it equally' answer: symmetric columns look tidy but the English column only has 51px of text space, so Horizontal and allocation break mid-word, while the four script columns get width they do not need."},"ranges":[[100,114],[52,64],[67,80],[60,70],[65,82]],"rationale":"This is a five-way lookup table whose pivot language (English) and Arabic carry by far the longest running text, so they should absorb the width while the Chinese, Japanese and Korean columns only need room for 2–3-character units plus an intact header. r1B keeps all five headers on one line, produces no mid-word splits and caps the tallest cell at three lines in the shortest table of the set (335px). It is also the only short design that leaves real slack at its two tightest points — English 83px of text space for the 76px word Horizontal, Arabic 50px for its 44px longest word — whereas r1C, r2B and r3B sit exactly on those thresholds where a font-rendering difference would trigger a split. The trade is that Chinese at 54px breaks 可读性 as 可读 / 性, but no feasible allocation at 360px avoids that.","principles":{"general":["Language/script names and short headers are scan anchors: never let a header break inside the name, even at the cost of body wrapping.","Size each column from its longest unbreakable token plus a few px of slack; widths that land exactly on a token width look fine in one render and split in the next.","Column width should track how much text each column actually carries, not symmetry — equal widths are only correct when the content is equal.","Judge the table by row rhythm as well as total height: one column forcing 4 lines distorts every row it touches."],"specific":["At 360px the four script columns are all forced below their one-line widths (62/107/73/112), so multi-line cells are unavoidable and the goal is minimising, not eliminating, them.","Three-character CJK compounds such as 可读性 need ~69px of column to stay whole; no design here provides it, so the 2+1 break is a fixed cost of this width.","The Korean column needs roughly 60px just to keep 한국어 on one line — the header, not the body text, sets its floor.","Arabic's 44px longest word sets a hard 65px floor for column 5; anything below causes a mid-word split in the right-to-left text."]},"tradeoffs":"A reasonable designer could prefer r1C: giving Arabic 79px instead of 71px measurably improves the longest right-to-left lines, at the cost of squeezing English to within 1px of its 76px word.
